answer: We model Sybil resistance via a dynamic opportunity-cost bond where each identity must stake collateral and solve a zero-knowledge verifiable delay function to emit a valid identity signal. In this distributed network, modeled as an island of honest nodes, any attempt at identity multiplication triggers a subgame-perfect slashing matrix. If an adversary attempts to split a single marble of capital into multiple identities, the expected utility is strictly negative, forcing a unique Nash equilibrium where honest participation dominates.
